title: A Framework for Fine-Grained Program Versioning
problem: Static dependence analysis is imprecise for compiler optimizations like vectorization. Loop versioning is loop-centric and ineffective for non-loop optimizations such as superword-level parallelism (SLP) vectorization.
motivation: Improving compiler optimization effectiveness through more precise runtime dependency analysis beyond existing loop-centric versioning techniques.
method: The framework allows client optimizations to specify groups of instructions or loops whose independence is desired but unprovable statically. The system duplicates these instructions and guards originals with runtime checks to guarantee independence; if checks fail, duplicated instructions execute instead. The approach is general-purpose and not tied to specific optimizations.
key_novelty: Fine-grained program versioning framework that extends beyond loop-level versioning to enable runtime dependency verification for arbitrary code regions and instructions.
contributions: A general fine-grained versioning framework applicable to any optimization, not tied to specific optimizations
Extended SLP vectorizer achieving 1.17× speedup on TSVC and 1.51× on PolyBench with minimal modifications
Demonstrated programs vectorizable only with fine-grained versioning but not with loop versioning alone
More aggressive redundant load elimination achieving 1.012× average speedup on SPEC 2017 FP (up to 1.064×)
primary_theme: Fine-grained runtime versioning for improved compiler optimizations
